owner_message_exact:
Scope clarification from the owner and originating audit session:

This phase exists to complete Datum’s transition from piecemeal rendering integrations to a shared rendering foundation. The GPU repair must address any remaining legacy responsibilities that prevent the shared architecture from delivering its intended behavior.

The audit established that pointer-only interaction still triggers full composed-scene GPU rendering. It did not establish a hardware limitation, a Wayland defect, or that every legacy integration is faulty.

Reassess your proposal against this objective:

1. Trace the pointer-to-render path and identify the actual ownership of invalidation, damage tracking, retained content, composition, and GPU resource lifetimes.
2. Identify legacy paths that bypass, duplicate, or undermine the shared architecture. Distinguish those from necessary platform/backend integration.
3. Propose how the shared renderer will own these responsibilities, with editors submitting changes through its contracts.
4. Name the superseded paths to remove and explain precisely which repeated GPU work disappears.
5. Account for correctness, 8× antialiasing, painter order, invalidation/recovery, and live/retiring GPU resources.

Your copy design may remain appropriate if it completes that architecture. Reassess it; do not discard sound work merely because of this clarification.

If complete DRM lifetime accounting is necessary but excluded by r1’s existing-observer scope, identify the required scope amendment. An artificially narrow proposal boundary must not become the stopping point for the overall repair. Explain separately whether the gap blocks a focused performance experiment, final qualification, or both.

The requested deliverable remains a concrete, reviewable solution proposal—not another sequence of speculative builds. Existing evidence should be reused. Implementation, builds, tests, and native runs still require the owner’s explicit approval of their scope.

Independent review is a recommendation, not owner ratification. Do not mark the GPU issue resolved until the approved implementation has demonstrated the required correctness and performance. CPU optimization remains deferred.
disposition: Planning-only reassessment toward shared rendering foundation. Preserve sound r1 copy reasoning; replace integration/proof boundaries with reviewable r2. Earlier execution selection is suspended. No implementation/build/test/native run under this clarification.
historical_attempt: capability-attempt.json records guard refusal before Cargo; production restored exactly. Temporary storage does not block source-only reassessment.
authority: Owner alone approves exact implementation and proof scope. Independent review is advisory; no issue resolution or performance acceptance.
